### Control C-2 — the eps -> 0 null test (kind: reachability)

At the smallest sweep point every non-Boussinesq term is O(1e-3) or smaller, so the two solvers must agree to within their own noise. What they disagree by THERE is a measured ceiling on any residual datum or property mismatch, and every separation reported above has to clear it.

### Control C-3 — the K0c anchor (kind: RECOGNITION, not reachability)

This control reads an already-published number back; it cannot fail in a way that is informative about K2e's own physics, and it is labelled accordingly. ### How the divergence scales with beta.dT — POST-HOC, gates nothing

Least squares of log D against log eps over the whole coarse sweep. This is a characterisation of the pre-registered quantities AFTER the fact. It decides nothing: every separation verdict above comes from the pre-registered thresholds alone. It is reported because the EXPONENT is the transferable part — it says how a divergence measured at one beta.dT carries to another, which a table of points does not.

| quantity | fit | exponent n | worst residual over the sweep % |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| D Nu_h % | 6.355 x (beta.dT)^1.968 | 1.968 | 4.65 |
| D u_max_star % | 24.91 x (beta.dT)^1.005 | 1.005 | 0.51 |
| D v_max_star % | 13.03 x (beta.dT)^1.022 | 1.022 | 0.93 |
| abs(theta_c) | 0.0343 x (beta.dT)^0.999 | 0.999 | 0.17 |
| abs(theta_vol) | 0.03532 x (beta.dT)^1.002 | 1.002 | 0.47 |
| abs(S_rms) | 0.0831 x (beta.dT)^1.002 | 1.002 | 0.39 |

Fitted over eps >= 0.05 only, the SAME cut for every quantity, chosen because below it every quantity sits on a solver-to-solver baseline floor of order 0.01 to 0.2 % that does not scale with eps: D(Nu_h) reads 0.010 % at both eps = 0.010 and eps = 0.033, which is a floor and not a trend. Fitting through a floor would flatten every exponent toward zero and misreport the scaling.

### Heat balance — reported because the specification requires it, and it is NOT evidence

Every K2e case is sealed and impermeable, so `heat_balance_closure_is_evidence_on_sealed_case: false` applies in full: the discrete equation forces the boundary terms to sum to zero at every iteration, converged or not. What a pass here still establishes is narrow — wrong properties, a wrong patch area, a wrong sign, a patch dropped from the sum.
